## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
Redblue lists are values, not iterators, so every helper that is lazy in other languages is materialised here, and the ones a program actually needs are simply missing. There is no chain to join two sequences, no zip to walk two together, no enumerate to pair with an index, no product to cross two sequences, no groupby to bucket, and no memoisation at all - so a recursive function that recomputes the same subproblem has no way to avoid it. phase-077 adds sort, reverse, zip, enumerate, filter and reduce to the list surface; this phase is the functions that are not list methods, and it is scoped to avoid overlapping phase-077.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Add the iteration helpers that are not list methods: chain, zip, enumerate, product, groupby, take, skip, and an lru_cache decorator usable on a function declaration. State plainly in SPEC.md which of these are lazy and which materialise, because on a list-valued language laziness has to be spelled out rather than assumed. Memoisation must be observable - a test counts calls, not just results, because a cache that never hits looks identical to one that works until the program gets slow.

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] chain, zip, enumerate, product, groupby, take and skip each return correct values on empty, single-element and multi-element inputs - all three shapes per function, asserted literally
- [ ] zip stops at the shorter input rather than padding with a missing value, and that rule is written in SPEC.md
- [ ] groupby returns groups in first-appearance order and groups keys by equality, asserted on a literal expected grouping
- [ ] an lru_cache-decorated recursive function is asserted to make fewer calls than the uncached version - the test counts calls, so a cache that never hits fails
- [ ] the cache evicts at its stated capacity and the test proves eviction by asserting the call count rises again after the bound is passed
- [ ] SPEC.md says for each helper whether it is lazy or materialising, and a test asserts that statement is not stale
- [ ] the tree-walker and the bytecode VM produce equal values for each helper, compared as data across both engines
- [ ] this phase does not re-add sort, reverse, zip or enumerate to the list surface - if phase-077 already added one of them, this phase extends it rather than defining a second spelling, and REPORT.md says which case applied
